title: Launch mortality and recovery scenario log
content:
Purpose:
This working log collects likely "mortality" scenarios for a staged product launch (canary -> beta -> general), tracks KPIs that surface progressive degradation, and prescribes recovery playbooks with owners and SLAs. Use this as the primary reference for the first 72 hours after rollout and as input to the formal postmortem.

Scope:
- Services: hosted API routes (text-generation, embeddings), routing mesh, caching layer, autoscaling pools (dedicated & hosted)
- Time window: -72h to +72h around each traffic ramp step
- Audience: product-ops, SRE, serving-runtime, solutions-eng

Quick primer (notes-to-self):
- "Mortality" = any condition where product feature is effectively unavailable for a user cohort (errors, timeouts, degraded quality causing rejections).
- Prioritize: availability > correctness > economics during first 24-48h.
- Keep communication short: status channel + summary cadence (T+0, T+1h, T+6h, T+24h).

KPI tracker (single-line rows for quick scan):
- Success rate (200s/all reqs): baseline 99.7% | alert 99.0% | critical 97.0% | owner: Marco Ruiz | playbook: throttle to canary, enable degraded-model fallback
- 95th latency (ms): baseline 320ms | alert 450ms | critical 800ms | owner: Tess Nguyen | playbook: reduce batch size, isolate large-seq traffic, enable region-fallback
- Token cost per 1k reqs (usd): baseline $3.40 | alert +25% | critical +50% | owner: Product Ops (Aisha) | playbook: swap to quantized variant, enable caching TTL increase
- Quality regression (eval set BLEU/ROUGE/metric): baseline 0.0% regression | alert >1.5% | critical >5% | owner: Ethan Clarke | playbook: rollback to previous model, disable auto-rollouts
- KV cache hit rate: baseline 12% | alert <8% | critical <4% | owner: Platform Eng | playbook: increase cache shards, flush partial caches, reroute reads

Top 7 mortality scenarios and immediate steps:
1) Global model OOM / crash on startup
   - Symptoms: rapid 500s across all zones, failed deploy events in infra logs.
   - Immediate: STOP rollout, revert to previous model version, scale-up small diagnostic fleet isolated from canary traffic.
   - Temporary comms: +status 'model-panic' channel.
2) Tokenization mismatch (edge cases) causing malformed outputs
   - Symptoms: sudden spike in parser errors, downstream consumer rejects.
   - Immediate: enable compatibility-tokenizer shim (traffic-level header), route failing requests to compat fallback.
3) Autoscaler thrash under burst traffic -> cold starts -> latency spike
   - Symptoms: 95th latency intermittently high, CPU/GPU spin-up logs noisy
   - Immediate: lock min-instances to canary pool, enable warm-up prefetch; update autoscaler cool-down to 10m.
4) Routing policy misconfiguration sends heavy batch jobs to low-memory nodes
   - Immediate: switch routing profile to conservative, drain affected nodes, evict large batch requests to dedicated resource pool.
5) Cost explosion due to runaway exponential retry loops in SDK clients
   - Immediate: set per-API-key rate limit, notify large customers, deploy transient feature-flag to reject retries with clear error.
6) Observability blindspot (missing traces for new route)
   - Immediate: enable verbose tracer, fallback to sample logging, create immediate dashboard tile for request lineage.
7) Quality regression discovered via synthetic evals
   - Immediate: divert 5% traffic to golden model, stop rollout, schedule hotfix/rollback decision within 2 hours.

Staffing and comms playbook (T+ relative times):
- T-24h: readiness email to owners, ensure runbook reachable, confirm on-call for product-ops & serving-runtime.
- T+0: Launch commander (Aisha) opens status thread; SRE lead posts infra snapshot; product lead posts adoption metrics baseline.
- T+1h: Short sync (10m) if any alert present.
- T+6h: Full checkpoint; decide if to proceed with ramp.
- T+24h: Stabilization review and handoff to steady-state ops.

Escalation matrix (one-line):
- Pager (SEV1): SRE on-call -> SRE manager -> Eng VP.
- Product Ops (feature impact): Product Ops on-call -> Product Director -> COO.

Decision heuristics for rollback vs mitigate (notes):
- Rollback iff user-visible failure rate > critical threshold OR quality regression affecting core customers within first 4h.
- Mitigate if localized to region/tier, cost-only issue, or latency spike with no data loss.

Post-launch artifacts to populate (deliverables checklist):
- Finalized timeline + actual timestamps (owner: Aisha)
- Incident log with play-by-play (owner: Marc)
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence table (owner: Tess)
- Metrics diff report (pre vs post) for success rate, latency, cost, quality (owner: Ethan)
- Postmortem published to CONFLUENCE and linked in Jira (owner: Product Ops)

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Add synthetic user profiles for long-tail tokenization cases (who: NLP Research).
- Confirm default autoscaler cool-down across clouds (who: Infra).
- Small experiment: pre-warm KV cache with top-100 prefix set before ramp (owner: Platform Eng).
- Validate rollback window for dedicated customers (legal/compliance).

Sign-off trail (in-progress):
- "I ACK this is our working canonical mortality log for rollouts v1" — Aisha Patel (11/12/2025)
- "Need to sync with SRE on autoscaler cool-down before next canary" — Marco Ruiz

Appendix: quick copy-paste snippets for status updates
- T+0 status: "Canary started: 1% of traffic. No alerts in first 10m. Monitoring active: success rate, 95th latency, cost delta, quality evals. Next check T+1h."
- If rollback: "Rollback initiated at T+X. Traffic reverted to v(prev). Incident timeline started. Postmortem owner: Product Ops."

End of working log.

(Notes: keep iterations in this doc rather than creating a separate one for each launch — append new run entries with date stamps and brief outcome summaries.)
